description.value: A pilot fMRI study investigated cerebral activation during script-driven imagery of self-injurious behavior in female patients with borderline personality disorder and healthy controls.

spans.text: This study compared the neural activation patterns of patients with BPD and healthy controls in response to the script-driven imagery of SIB.

script-driven imagery

description.value: One standard script describing the circumstances and execution of an act of SIB was presented in five sections.

spans.text: One standard script describing the circumstances and execution of an act of SIB was developed in first person singular, comprising the following five sections: i) neutral sequence (baseline), ii) trigger situation, iii) emotional and cognitive reactions, iv) SIB and v) relaxation.
neutral
neutral sequence (baseline)

description.value: A neutral baseline script sequence describing a woman on a shopping tour, lasting approximately 120 seconds. Participants were instructed to imagine the description as vividly as possible; the condition served as the baseline comparison.

spans.text: The neutral section describes a woman on a shopping tour and lasts about 120 s.
trigger

description.value: A 77-second script section describing a trigger situation in which a woman watches a dispute between a mother and her child. Participants listened and imagined the description as vividly as possible.

spans.text: The trigger situation (77 s) describes the woman watching a dispute between a mother and her child.
reactions

description.value: A 74-second script section describing emotional and cognitive reactions to the trigger, including ruminations about similar negative experiences with the woman's mother. Participants listened and imagined the description as vividly as possible.

spans.text: During the following section (74 s), the emotional and cognitive reactions including the person’s ruminations concerning similar negative experiences with her mother are delineated.
SIB

description.value: A 64-second script section describing preparation for and performance of a typical act of self-injurious behavior, including cutting. Participants listened and imagined the act as vividly as possible.

spans.text: Subsequently, a typical act of SIB is described (64 s), including preparation and the cutting itself.
relaxation

description.value: A 77-second script section describing relaxation and the self-injury-induced decrease in aversive inner tension. Participants listened and imagined the description as vividly as possible.

spans.text: The last section of the script, relaxation (77 s), includes the SIB -induced decrease in aversive inner tension.
We employed script-driven imagery to induce emotional distress.
